Types
- text — Textual content. Kind is set from the file extension (md, txt, csv, html, ...). Kind is a hint by default; strict is a no-op for text (plain vs markdown is not detectable from content). (e.g. Hello, world)
- number — A number, whole or decimal, of any size. Its kind is the precision it is held in (int, long, decimal, double, …). (e.g. 42)
- bool — True or false. (e.g. true)
- list — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- dict — Named values: each key holds a value of any type. (e.g. {"name":"Ada","age":36})
- variable — A variable, named between % signs, that holds a value. (e.g. %user%)
- item
- action (e.g. goal.call(Name="Show"))
- choice<actor> — one of: system, user
- duration — A length of time, written in ISO 8601 (PT5M is five minutes). (e.g. PT5M)
- choice<direction> — one of: Input, Output, Bidirectional
- path — Where a file, a folder or a web resource is: a path in the app, an absolute path, or a URL. (e.g. /docs/readme.md)

Settings
- %!build%(cache: bool = true, files: list = [])

## variable.set(Name: variable, Value: item, Type?: item, AsDefault?: bool = false)
Assign a value to a named variable, optionally coercing to a type or setting only when unset
Name — the variable to set, with its % signs. A `(<kind>)` written after it is not part of the name: it is the Type.
Value — the value as the step writes it, typed as what it is (a quoted date is a date, "42" a number, a label stays text). After another action in the same step it is %!data%.
Type — only when the step forces a type: `as <type>` or `(<kind>)`.
AsDefault — true when the step says "set default", "default to" or "only if unset"; the variable keeps a value it already has.

- `set %x% = …` is one variable.set.
- `<action>, write to %x%` is that action followed by variable.set(Name=%x%, Value=%!data%) — its own action, never a modifier, and without a Type.

## channel.set(Name: text, Goal: action, Actor?: choice<actor>, Buffer?: number, Timeout?: duration, Mime?: text, Encoding?: text, Direction?: choice<direction>, Encryption?: variable, Signing?: variable)
Register or replace a named channel backed by a goal call. Always upserts.
Name — the channel's name: the quoted text, or `output`, `error`, `input`.
Goal — the goal that backs the channel: a goal.call action, the goal named after `call` or `as`.
Actor — the actor whose channel it is, only when the step names one (`set system input channel …`).
Buffer — the channel's buffer size, only when the step gives one.
Timeout — how long one message may take, only when the step gives one (a duration, `PT30S`).
Mime, Encoding — the content type and text encoding, only when the step names them.
Direction — `input`, `output` or `bidirectional`, only when the step says; the names input and output decide it themselves.
Encryption, Signing — the variables holding the keys, only when the step names them.

## goal.call(Name: text, Parameter?: list, Actor?: choice<actor>, Parallel?: bool = false)
Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
Name — the goal to call, copied exactly as the step writes it: `Goal`, `Folder/Goal`, `/system/builder/Goal`. Never an action name like `goal.call`.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the goal name is one argument, its value as written. Left out when the step passes none.
Actor — the actor the goal runs on, only when the step names one (`on actor "system"`, `as user`). Not because the goal is a system goal, a sub-goal or a recovery.
Parallel — true only when the step says the call may run beside others.

- The arguments belong to the called goal; they are never properties of goal.call.
- `foreach %list%, call X item=%y%` is loop.foreach, then goal.call with `item` as its argument.

## build.load(Path?: path = .)
Load the app-level build context from a directory path
Path — the app's folder; left out for the current one.

## build.goals(Path: path)
Load all goal files from a directory for processing by the builder
Path — the folder whose .goal files are loaded.

## loop.foreach(Collection: item, Item?: variable = item, Key?: variable)
Iterate over Collection, binding each element to Item (and its key or index to Key) and executing the remaining step actions
Collection — the list or dict to walk.
Item — the variable each element is bound to; %item% unless the step names another (`as %product%`).
Key — the variable the key or index is bound to, only when the step names one (`with key %sku%`).

- The work done per element is its own action after loop.foreach in the step's list (usually goal.call), never inside it.
- `name=%item%` after the called goal is an argument of that goal.call, not a foreach property.

## file.save(Path: path, Value: item)
Write Value to a file at Path, creating directories as needed. Saving a `%!…%` setting (`save %!llm%`) is not this: that is setting.save.
Path — the file to write, as the step writes it (`to file '…'`).
Value — what to write: `save %x% to file …` saves %x%.

## build.appSave()
Persist the built app artifact to disk after a successful build run

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Build. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: set default %path% = "/"
step 1: set default %!build.cache% = true
step 2: set default %!build.summary% = true
step 3: set channel "builder" call BuilderChannel

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- assert: Test assertions: demand that something holds and fail the step with a descriptive error when it does not. A step that DEMANDS an outcome is this module; a step that merely asks whether something holds, and branches or keeps the answer, is the condition module. Only one of the two is ever used in a step, never both.
- build: Builder internals: load, merge, validate, and save goal and step data during the build pipeline
- callback: Run a callback — resume execution from the Data's Snapshot.
- channel: Manage channels (set, remove) for the current or named actor.
  e.g. `set output channel as MyGoal`
  e.g. `set error channel as ErrorHandler`
  e.g. `set channel "builder" call BuilderChannel`
- code: Manage the provider registry: list, load, remove, and change defaults for signing, crypto, etc.
- condition: Comparisons: ask whether something holds — equal, greater, contains, starts with, empty — and either branch on the answer (if/elseif/else) or keep it. Any yes/no question belongs here, whatever it is about: whether a list holds an item, whether text starts with something, whether a number is bigger. The subject's own module is not involved just because the question is about its contents. What follows the comparison is an ordinary action — call a goal, return from the goal (`if %done%, return`), write out, keep the answer in a variable — and is that action's own module.
  e.g. `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
  e.g. `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
  e.g. `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
  e.g. `check if %content% is empty, write out "nothing here"`
  e.g. `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty`
  e.g. `if %flag% is true, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
- crypto: Cryptographic hashing and hash verification using configurable algorithms
  e.g. `hash %content%, write to %hash%`
  e.g. `hash %content% with sha256, write to %hash%`
  e.g. `verify %content% against %hash%, write to %isValid%`
- debug: Write tag metadata onto the current call frame for diagnostics
- environment: Run a goal, step, or action on a specified actor
- error: Throw an error from a step (handling one is on.error)
- file: Read, write, copy, move, delete, and list files through the configured filesystem abstraction. A `%!path%` is a setting, never a file: `save %!llm%` saves a setting, which is the setting module.
  e.g. `check if file.txt exists, write to %fileInfo%`
  e.g. `list files in docs/ recursive, write to %files%`
  e.g. `list files in %folder%`
  e.g. `read file.txt, write to %content%`
  e.g. `read 'config/settings.json'`
- goal: Goals: call another goal (`call X`, on its own or as the body of an if/foreach/on-error clause) and return from the current goal
  e.g. `call Finalize`
  e.g. `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
  e.g. `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `return %result%`
  e.g. `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
  e.g. `if %items% is empty, return`
- http: HTTP client: send requests, and upload or download files
- identity: Manage cryptographic identities: create, list, set default, rename, archive, and export keys
- list: Inspect and manipulate in-memory lists: add, remove, sort, search, split, join, and group items
  e.g. `add 'apple' to %fruits%`
  e.g. `add %newItem% to %items%`
  e.g. `add {name: "Ada", age: 30} to %users%`
  e.g. `add {goal: %goal.Name%, index: %step.Index%, response: %compileResult%} to %trace.stepPasses%`
  e.g. `insert 'first' at position 0 in %items%`
- llm: Send prompts to an LLM and receive structured or streamed responses, with optional tool use; or ask a decision service typed yes/no and pick-one questions about a shared state
  e.g. `system: analyze sentiment, user: %comment%, schema: {sentiment: string}, write to %result%`
  e.g. `ask the llm "summarise %text%", write to %summary%`
- loop: Iterate over a collection, executing the remaining step actions once per item
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call ProcessItem item=%item%`

  e.g. `foreach %products% as %product%, call Handle`

  e.g. `set %total% = %total% + %item%`
  e.g. `add %price% and %tax%, write to %sum%`
- mock: Test mocking: intercept actions by pattern and replace them with fixed responses or spy on calls
- module: Load and unload external module DLLs at runtime to extend the available action catalog
- on: Events: what runs when something happens — a goal call bound before or after an item's event (each goal or step starting, an action starting, a channel writing, reading or asking), cancelling the event from inside it, taking a binding off; and the clauses of the action before them: on error (retry it, run a recovery, or carry on), on cache (keep its result), on timeout (give it a deadline)

- output: Send text or data to a channel (console, logger, audit, etc.)
  e.g. `ask user 'what's your name?', write to %name%`

  e.g. `print %result%`
  e.g. `write %error.Message% to "errors" channel`
- setting: Keeps an actor's settings for the runs after this one. A setting is read as `%!path%` (`%!app.goal.list.setting.os%`, `%!llm.cache%`) and changed for this run with `set %!path% = value` — that is the variable module, never this one. This module only saves a setting whole as the actor's row, or removes that row.
- signing: Sign and verify data payloads using pluggable cryptographic providers. Only a step whose work IS signing or verifying belongs here. Another action's step may mention being signed or unsigned — a request sent unsigned, a file saved signed — and that is an option of that action, not this module.
- snapshot: Resume a captured snapshot — restore its Variables and CallStack and re-enter the step where execution was suspended (typically read back from a `.snapshot` file).
  e.g. `resume %snap%`
  e.g. `resume %snapshot%`
- test: Discover, run, and report on PLang test goals with tag filtering and coverage tracking

- goal.call: Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
  e.g. `call Finalize`

s0_variable.set.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `variable.set`?

criteria.true: the step sets a variable or keeps a result in one: `set %x% = 5`, `set default %x% = …`, `…, write to %x%`

s0_goal.call.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `goal.call`?

criteria.true: the step itself calls a goal now, alone or inside its condition or loop: `call SendMail to=%x%`, `if %n% > 5, call Big`, `foreach %list%, call X`, `call Compile, on error call Fix` (it calls Compile)
criteria.false: the step calls no goal now; the goal behind a channel or an event, named to run later, is not called by the step

s0_loop.foreach.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `loop.foreach`?

criteria.true: the step repeats something for each item of a collection: `foreach %list%, call X item=%item%`, `for each %order% in %orders%, …`
criteria.false: the step does its work once; a list it only reads, counts or passes along is not repeated over

s0_goal.return.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `goal.return`?

criteria.true: the step returns from the goal, now or as the body of its if: `return %result%`, `if %done%, return`
criteria.false: the step doesn't return; calling another goal is not returning

s0_output.write.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `output.write`?

criteria.true: the step shows or writes something out, to the user or to a named channel: `write out "Hello"`, `show %message%`, `write %x% to "log" channel`
criteria.false: the step shows nothing; `…, write to %x%` keeps a value in a variable, it is not output

s0_on.error.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `on.error`?

criteria.true: the step says what happens when it fails: `…, on error call X`, `…, on error retry 3 times`
criteria.false: the step says nothing about failing; throwing an error (`throw "…"`) is not handling one

s0_on.cache.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `on.cache`?

criteria.true: the step keeps its result for a while, so running it again is served without redoing the work: `…, cache for 5 minutes`, `…, cache 1 hour`
criteria.false: the step says nothing about keeping its result; saving to a file or a variable is not caching

criteria.false: the step sets no deadline; waiting or sleeping for a time (`sleep 1000 ms`) is not a timeout

s0_condition.if.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `condition.if`?

criteria.true: the step tests something and does its work only when it holds: `if %x% > 5, …`, `if %list% is empty`
criteria.false: the step tests nothing

s0_file.read.instructions: Step 0 is `set default %path% = "/"`. Does step 0 use `file.read`?

criteria.true: the step reads a file's content: `read 'notes.txt'`, `read file %path%, write to %text%`
criteria.false: the step reads no file; saving, listing or deleting a file is not reading it

s1_@module.instructions: Step 1 of this goal is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Which plang module does the main work of step 1?

s1_variable.set.instructions: Step 1 is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Does step 1 use `variable.set`?

criteria.true: the step sets a variable or keeps a result in one: `set %x% = 5`, `set default %x% = …`, `…, write to %x%`
criteria.false: the step keeps no value in a variable

s1_goal.call.instructions: Step 1 is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Does step 1 use `goal.call`?

criteria.true: the step itself calls a goal now, alone or inside its condition or loop: `call SendMail to=%x%`, `if %n% > 5, call Big`, `foreach %list%, call X`, `call Compile, on error call Fix` (it calls Compile)
criteria.false: the step calls no goal now; the goal behind a channel or an event, named to run later, is not called by the step

s1_loop.foreach.instructions: Step 1 is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Does step 1 use `loop.foreach`?

criteria.true: the step repeats something for each item of a collection: `foreach %list%, call X item=%item%`, `for each %order% in %orders%, …`
criteria.false: the step does its work once; a list it only reads, counts or passes along is not repeated over

s1_goal.return.instructions: Step 1 is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Does step 1 use `goal.return`?

criteria.true: the step returns from the goal, now or as the body of its if: `return %result%`, `if %done%, return`
criteria.false: the step doesn't return; calling another goal is not returning

s1_output.write.instructions: Step 1 is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Does step 1 use `output.write`?

criteria.true: the step shows or writes something out, to the user or to a named channel: `write out "Hello"`, `show %message%`, `write %x% to "log" channel`
criteria.false: the step shows nothing; `…, write to %x%` keeps a value in a variable, it is not output

s1_on.error.instructions: Step 1 is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Does step 1 use `on.error`?

criteria.true: the step says what happens when it fails: `…, on error call X`, `…, on error retry 3 times`
criteria.false: the step says nothing about failing; throwing an error (`throw "…"`) is not handling one

s1_on.cache.instructions: Step 1 is `set default %!build.cache% = true`. Does step 1 use `on.cache`?

criteria.false: the step says nothing about keeping its result; saving to a file or a variable is not caching

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Build. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: set default %path% = "/"
step 1: set default %!build.cache% = true
step 2: set default %!build.summary% = true
step 3: set channel "builder" call BuilderChannel
step 4: call EmitBuildEvent kind="build-path", path=%path%
step 5: build.load, write to %app%
step 6: build.goals path=%path%, write to %goals%
step 7: call EmitBuildEvent kind="goals-found", goals=%goals%
step 8: foreach %goals%, call BuildGoal goal=%item%
step 9: save %traceGoals% to file '/.build/traces/%!trace.id%/manifest.json'
step 10: build.appSave

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- build: Builder internals: load, merge, validate, and save goal and step data during the build pipeline
  action build.appSave: Persist the built app artifact to disk after a successful build run
  action build.fold: Place the steps indented under a condition into that condition's child, in the goal and its sub-goals
  action build.goals: Load all goal files from a directory for processing by the builder
  action build.goalsSave: Save a built goal's .pr file to disk, completing the build for that goal
  action build.load: Load the app-level build context from a directory path
  action build.match: Check the LLM's answer against the goal's steps, one entry per step, before the steps take their actions from it
  action build.pick: Hand a decider answer to each step of a goal, which works out the actions the decider picked for it
- channel: Manage channels (set, remove) for the current or named actor.
  e.g. `set output channel as MyGoal`
  e.g. `set error channel as ErrorHandler`
  e.g. `set channel "builder" call BuilderChannel`
  action channel.remove: Remove a channel by name. Default channels (output/error/input) cannot be removed.
  action channel.set: Register or replace a named channel backed by a goal call. Always upserts.
    examples: Step text: `set output channel as MyGoal`
Properties: `{"Name": "output", "Goal": {"module": "goal", "name": "call", "property": [{"name": "Name", "value": "MyGoal"}]}}`

Step text: `set error channel as ErrorHandler`
Properties: `{"Name": "error", "Goal": {"module": "goal", "name": "call", "property": [{"name": "Name", "value": "ErrorHandler"}]}}`

Step text: `set channel "builder" call BuilderChannel`
Properties: `{"Name": "builder", "Goal": {"module": "goal", "name": "call", "property": [{"name": "Name", "value": "BuilderChannel"}]}}` — the channel name is the quoted literal; the goal is the one named after `call`.

The channel name (output, error, input, or any custom literal) is always a bare string, never a
%variable%. `Goal` is the `goal.call` action whose goal backs the channel — the same shape as any
other goal.call.
- file: Read, write, copy, move, delete, and list files through the configured filesystem abstraction. A `%!path%` is a setting, never a file: `save %!llm%` saves a setting, which is the setting module.
  e.g. `check if file.txt exists, write to %fileInfo%`
  e.g. `list files in docs/ recursive, write to %files%`
  e.g. `list files in %folder%`
  e.g. `read file.txt, write to %content%`
  e.g. `read 'config/settings.json'`
  action file.copy: Copy a file or folder from Source to Destination, optionally overwriting and including subfolders
  action file.delete: Delete a file or directory at Path, optionally recursively or ignoring missing targets
  action file.exists: Check whether a file or directory exists at Path and return file info
    examples: Step text: `check if file.txt exists, write to %fileInfo%`
Properties: `{"Path": "file.txt"}`
  action file.list: List files in a directory matching an optional glob pattern, optionally recursing into subdirectories
    examples: Step text: `list files in docs/ recursive, write to %files%`
Properties: `{"Path": "docs/", "Recursive": true}`

Step text: `list files in %folder%`
Properties: `{"Path": "%folder%"}` — `Recursive` is absent because the step does not ask for it.
  action file.move: Move or rename a file from Source to Destination, optionally overwriting the target
  action file.read: Read a file's content; optionally resolve %var% patterns in the text before returning
    examples: Step text: `read file.txt, write to %content%`
Properties: `{"Path": "file.txt"}` — the trailing `write to %content%` is its own action.

Step text: `read 'config/settings.json'`
Properties: `{"Path": "config/settings.json"}`
  action file.save: Write Value to a file at Path, creating directories as needed. Saving a `%!…%` setting (`save %!llm%`) is not this: that is setting.save.
- goal: Goals: call another goal (`call X`, on its own or as the body of an if/foreach/on-error clause) and return from the current goal
  e.g. `call Finalize`
  e.g. `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
  e.g. `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `return %result%`
  e.g. `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
  e.g. `if %items% is empty, return`
  action goal.call: Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
    examples: `goal.call` runs another goal. It is the action behind `call X` wherever that clause appears — on its own, as the body of a condition, as the body of a loop, or inside an error handler. `Name` is the goal; each named argument after it is one row in `Parameter`.

Step text: `call Finalize`
Properties: `{"Name": "Finalize"}`

Step text: `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
Properties: `{"Name": "ProcessOrder", "Parameter": [{"name": "id", "value": "%orderId%"}, {"name": "retries", "value": 3}]}`

Step text: `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
Properties: `{"Name": "/system/builder/EmitBuildEvent", "Parameter": [{"name": "kind", "value": "done"}]}` — a path-qualified name is still just the name.

Step text: `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
Properties: `{"Name": "MarkBig"}` — the condition is its own action; this one is only the call.

  action goal.return: Return early from the current goal, propagating Data as the goal result
    examples: Step text: `return %result%`
Properties: `{"Data": "%result%"}`

Step text: `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
Properties: `{"Data": "%goal.Cache%"}` — the return is the if's body: it goes inside the if's `{ }`, `condition.if(Left=%goal.IsCached%) { goal.return(Data=%goal.Cache%) }`, never beside the if.

Properties: `{}` — a return that names no value; the body of the if: `condition.if(Left=%items%, Operator="isempty") { goal.return() }`.
- output: Send text or data to a channel (console, logger, audit, etc.)

  e.g. `ask 'Allow access? (y/n/a)', write to %answer%`

  e.g. `show %message% to the user`
  e.g. `print %result%`
  e.g. `write %error.Message% to "errors" channel`

    examples: Step text: `ask user 'what's your name?', write to %name%`
Properties: `{"Question": "what's your name?"}` — the trailing `write to %name%` is its own action.

Step text: `ask 'Allow access? (y/n/a)', write to %answer%`
Properties: `{"Question": "Allow access? (y/n/a)"}`

- setting: Keeps an actor's settings for the runs after this one. A setting is read as `%!path%` (`%!app.goal.list.setting.os%`, `%!llm.cache%`) and changed for this run with `set %!path% = value` — that is the variable module, never this one. This module only saves a setting whole as the actor's row, or removes that row.

These actions are offered by name:
- variable.set: Assign a value to a named variable, optionally coercing to a type or setting only when unset
- goal.call: Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
- output.write: Write Data to a named channel — defaults to the actor's output channel.
- on.error: Answer when the action before it fails; optionally retry it, run a recovery, or carry on past the error
- condition.if: Evaluate a condition and execute the then-branch actions; pair with elseif/else for full branching
- file.read: Read a file's content; optionally resolve %var% patterns in the text before returning
- file.save: Write Value to a file at Path, creating directories as needed. Saving a `%!…%` setting (`save %!llm%`) is not this: that is setting.save.
- error.throw: Immediately fail the step with a structured error message, status code, and optional key
- file.delete: Delete a file or directory at Path, optionally recursively or ignoring missing targets
- signing.sign: Sign a data payload and return a signed envelope via the configured signing provider
- list.count: Return the number of items in the list
- math.add: Add A and B together and return the numeric result
- loop.foreach: Iterate over Collection, binding each element to Item (and its key or index to Key) and executing the remaining step actions
- signing.verify: Verify a signed envelope against expected contracts and headers
- on.cache: Cache the result of the action before it for a duration; a cached result answers in its place and the work is skipped

Types
- text — Textual content. Kind is set from the file extension (md, txt, csv, html, ...). Kind is a hint by default; strict is a no-op for text (plain vs markdown is not detectable from content). (e.g. Hello, world)
- number — A number, whole or decimal, of any size. Its kind is the precision it is held in (int, long, decimal, double, …). (e.g. 42)
- bool — True or false. (e.g. true)
- list — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- dict — Named values: each key holds a value of any type. (e.g. {"name":"Ada","age":36})
- choice<actor> — one of: system, user
- variable — A variable, named between % signs, that holds a value. (e.g. %user%)
- item
- duration — A length of time, written in ISO 8601 (PT5M is five minutes). (e.g. PT5M)
- choice<errororder> — one of: GoalFirst, RetryFirst
- list<action> — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- choice<overflow> — one of: Promote, Throw
- choice<precision> — one of: Error, Double, Decimal
- path — Where a file, a folder or a web resource is: a path in the app, an absolute path, or a URL. (e.g. /docs/readme.md)
- goal — A goal: a named list of steps, called by its name. (e.g. Show)

## goal.call(Name: text, Parameter?: list, Actor?: choice<actor>, Parallel?: bool = false)
Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
Name — the goal to call, copied exactly as the step writes it: `Goal`, `Folder/Goal`, `/system/builder/Goal`. Never an action name like `goal.call`.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the goal name is one argument, its value as written. Left out when the step passes none.
Actor — the actor the goal runs on, only when the step names one (`on actor "system"`, `as user`). Not because the goal is a system goal, a sub-goal or a recovery.
Parallel — true only when the step says the call may run beside others.

- The arguments belong to the called goal; they are never properties of goal.call.
- `foreach %list%, call X item=%y%` is loop.foreach, then goal.call with `item` as its argument.

## variable.set(Name: variable, Value: item, Type?: item, AsDefault?: bool = false)
Assign a value to a named variable, optionally coercing to a type or setting only when unset
Name — the variable to set, with its % signs. A `(<kind>)` written after it is not part of the name: it is the Type.
Value — the value as the step writes it, typed as what it is (a quoted date is a date, "42" a number, a label stays text). After another action in the same step it is %!data%.
Type — only when the step forces a type: `as <type>` or `(<kind>)`.
AsDefault — true when the step says "set default", "default to" or "only if unset"; the variable keeps a value it already has.

- `set %x% = …` is one variable.set.
- `<action>, write to %x%` is that action followed by variable.set(Name=%x%, Value=%!data%) — its own action, never a modifier, and without a Type.

## on.error(StatusCode?: number, Key?: text, Message?: text, RetryCount?: number, RetryOver?: duration, Order?: choice<errororder>, IgnoreError?: bool = false, Recovery?: list<action>)
Answer when the action before it fails; optionally retry it, run a recovery, or carry on past the error
A clause: it comes right after the action it is a clause of, as the next action of the step. It answers when that action fails — after the attempt, so an `on.timeout` deadline is past and an `on.cache` stores only real work.

Recovery — the actions to run when the action fails: what the step says after "on error" (or "if it fails", in any language).
StatusCode — handle only errors with this status code.
Key — handle only errors with this key (`on error key "NotFound"`).
Message — handle only errors whose message contains this text.
RetryCount — how many times to run the action again ("retry 3 times"); each retry is a fresh attempt.
RetryOver — the time the retries are spread over, a duration ("over 30 seconds" → "PT30S").
Order — GoalFirst when the step runs the recovery before retrying ("call X, then retry"); left out for the default, retrying first ("retry 3 times, then call X").
IgnoreError — true when the step says to carry on past the error.

- The recovery runs only on error: it is never also an action of the step.
- StatusCode, Key and Message filter which errors are handled; they never hold what the recovery does. Left out when the step names no filter.
- Several on.error clauses are asked in the order written; the first that matches takes the error, and the others never see it.

## loop.foreach(Collection: item, Item?: variable = item, Key?: variable)
Iterate over Collection, binding each element to Item (and its key or index to Key) and executing the remaining step actions
Collection — the list or dict to walk.
Item — the variable each element is bound to; %item% unless the step names another (`as %product%`).
Key — the variable the key or index is bound to, only when the step names one (`with key %sku%`).

- The work done per element is its own action after loop.foreach in the step's list (usually goal.call), never inside it.
- `name=%item%` after the called goal is an argument of that goal.call, not a foreach property.

## math.subtract(A: item, B: item, Overflow?: choice<overflow> = Promote, Precision?: choice<precision> = Error)
Subtract B from A and return the numeric result
A, B — the two numbers: the result is A − B.
Overflow — only when the step says what to do when an integer overflows: Promote widens it, Throw fails.
Precision — only when the step says how to mix a decimal and a floating-point number.

## math.divide(A: item, B: item, Overflow?: choice<overflow> = Promote, Precision?: choice<precision> = Error)
Divide A by B and return the result; always leaves the integer track (7/2 → 3.5, never 3 — use math.intdiv for truncating integer division). Fails on division by zero.
A, B — the two numbers: the result is A ÷ B.
Overflow — only when the step says what to do when an integer overflows: Promote widens it, Throw fails.
Precision — only when the step says how to mix a decimal and a floating-point number.

## file.save(Path: path, Value: item)
Write Value to a file at Path, creating directories as needed. Saving a `%!…%` setting (`save %!llm%`) is not this: that is setting.save.
Path — the file to write, as the step writes it (`to file '…'`).
Value — what to write: `save %x% to file …` saves %x%.

## list.add(ListName: variable, Value: item, AtIndex?: number = -1)
Append or insert a value into a list variable at an optional index
ListName — the list variable to add to, with its % signs: in `add X to %list%` it is %list%.
Value — what to add, as the step writes it; a `{…}` or `[…]` literal is one value, typed dict or list.
AtIndex — the position to insert at, only when the step names one ("at position 2"); otherwise it appends.

- `add X to %list%` has no variable.set: %list% is the target, not a result to keep.

## build.fold(Goal: goal)
Place the steps indented under a condition into that condition's child, in the goal and its sub-goals
Goal — the goal whose indented steps are placed into their conditions: `Goal=%goal%` as the step writes it.

## build.goalsSave(Goal: goal)
Save a built goal's .pr file to disk, completing the build for that goal
Goal — the built goal whose .pr is saved: `Goal=%goal%` as the step writes it.

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Start. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="goalHeader", goal=%goal%
step 1: set %buildStart% = %Now.Ticks%
step 2: set %trace% = {"id": "%!trace.id%", "timestamp": "%Now%", "goal": %goal%, "menu": null, "subGoals": [], "durationMs": 0}
step 3: call Compile, on error call HandleBuildFailure
step 4: set %trace.menu% = %menu%

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- assert: Test assertions: demand that something holds and fail the step with a descriptive error when it does not. A step that DEMANDS an outcome is this module; a step that merely asks whether something holds, and branches or keeps the answer, is the condition module. Only one of the two is ever used in a step, never both.
- build: Builder internals: load, merge, validate, and save goal and step data during the build pipeline
- callback: Run a callback — resume execution from the Data's Snapshot.
- channel: Manage channels (set, remove) for the current or named actor.
  e.g. `set output channel as MyGoal`
  e.g. `set error channel as ErrorHandler`
  e.g. `set channel "builder" call BuilderChannel`
- code: Manage the provider registry: list, load, remove, and change defaults for signing, crypto, etc.
- condition: Comparisons: ask whether something holds — equal, greater, contains, starts with, empty — and either branch on the answer (if/elseif/else) or keep it. Any yes/no question belongs here, whatever it is about: whether a list holds an item, whether text starts with something, whether a number is bigger. The subject's own module is not involved just because the question is about its contents. What follows the comparison is an ordinary action — call a goal, return from the goal (`if %done%, return`), write out, keep the answer in a variable — and is that action's own module.
  e.g. `compare %a% > %b%, write to %isGreater%`
  e.g. `check if %myList% contains 20, write to %has20%`
  e.g. `check if %name% starts with "plang", write to %isPlang%`
  e.g. `check if %content% is empty, write out "nothing here"`
  e.g. `else if %a% > 5, write 'mid'`
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty`
  e.g. `if %flag% is true, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
- crypto: Cryptographic hashing and hash verification using configurable algorithms
  e.g. `hash %content%, write to %hash%`
  e.g. `hash %content% with sha256, write to %hash%`
  e.g. `verify %content% against %hash%, write to %isValid%`
- debug: Write tag metadata onto the current call frame for diagnostics
- environment: Run a goal, step, or action on a specified actor
- error: Throw an error from a step (handling one is on.error)
- file: Read, write, copy, move, delete, and list files through the configured filesystem abstraction. A `%!path%` is a setting, never a file: `save %!llm%` saves a setting, which is the setting module.
  e.g. `check if file.txt exists, write to %fileInfo%`
  e.g. `list files in docs/ recursive, write to %files%`
  e.g. `list files in %folder%`
  e.g. `read file.txt, write to %content%`
  e.g. `read 'config/settings.json'`
- goal: Goals: call another goal (`call X`, on its own or as the body of an if/foreach/on-error clause) and return from the current goal
  e.g. `call Finalize`
  e.g. `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
  e.g. `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `return %result%`
  e.g. `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
  e.g. `if %items% is empty, return`
- http: HTTP client: send requests, and upload or download files
- identity: Manage cryptographic identities: create, list, set default, rename, archive, and export keys
- list: Inspect and manipulate in-memory lists: add, remove, sort, search, split, join, and group items
  e.g. `add 'apple' to %fruits%`
  e.g. `add %newItem% to %items%`
  e.g. `add {name: "Ada", age: 30} to %users%`
  e.g. `add {goal: %goal.Name%, index: %step.Index%, response: %compileResult%} to %trace.stepPasses%`
  e.g. `insert 'first' at position 0 in %items%`
- llm: Send prompts to an LLM and receive structured or streamed responses, with optional tool use; or ask a decision service typed yes/no and pick-one questions about a shared state
  e.g. `system: analyze sentiment, user: %comment%, schema: {sentiment: string}, write to %result%`
  e.g. `ask the llm "summarise %text%", write to %summary%`
- loop: Iterate over a collection, executing the remaining step actions once per item
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call ProcessItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `foreach %rows%, write out %row%`
  e.g. `foreach %products% as %product%, call Handle`
  e.g. `foreach %prices% as %price% with key %sku%, write out "%sku%: %price%"`
- math: Arithmetic operations on numeric values: add, subtract, multiply, divide, round, and more
  e.g. `set %total% = %total% + %item%`
  e.g. `add %price% and %tax%, write to %sum%`
- mock: Test mocking: intercept actions by pattern and replace them with fixed responses or spy on calls
- module: Load and unload external module DLLs at runtime to extend the available action catalog
- on: Events: what runs when something happens — a goal call bound before or after an item's event (each goal or step starting, an action starting, a channel writing, reading or asking), cancelling the event from inside it, taking a binding off; and the clauses of the action before them: on error (retry it, run a recovery, or carry on), on cache (keep its result), on timeout (give it a deadline)
  e.g. `get https://example.com/rates, cache for 5 minutes, write to %rates%`
  e.g. `read %path%, cache 1 hour sliding`
  e.g. `call LoadUser id=%id%, cache 10 minutes by "user-%id%"`
  e.g. `skip action and set "overridden" as result`
  e.g. `cancel it, value = %mockResponse%`
  e.g. `read file.txt, on error call HandleMissing`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `save %doc%, on error key Conflict, write out "already exists"`
  e.g. `read %path%, on error 404, write out "missing"`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times over 30 seconds`
  e.g. `write out "hi", on error ignore`
  e.g. `call Save, on error retry 2 times, then call Rollback`
  e.g. `call Save, on error call Rollback first, then retry 2 times`
  e.g. `render %template%, on error 404 call Fallback then retry, write to %text%`
  e.g. `before each goal call LogBefore`
  e.g. `after step call TrackAfterStep`
  e.g. `before action file.read call OverrideFileRead`

  e.g. `call Import, timeout 2 minutes, on error call Alert`

  e.g. `ask user 'what's your name?', write to %name%`
  e.g. `ask 'Allow access? (y/n/a)', write to %answer%`
  e.g. `write out "Welcome back, %user.name%"`
  e.g. `show %message% to the user`
  e.g. `print %result%`
  e.g. `write %error.Message% to "errors" channel`

A setting is read as `%!path%` (`%!app.goal.list.setting.os%`, `%!llm.cache%`) and changed for this run with `set %!path% = value` — that is the variable module, never this one. This module only saves a setting whole as the actor's row, or removes that row.

Another action's step may mention being signed or unsigned — a request sent unsigned, a file saved signed — and that is an option of that action, not this module.

  e.g. `resume %snapshot%`

  e.g. `discover tests in '_fixtures', pattern='*.fixture.goal'`

  e.g. `sleep 2 seconds`
  e.g. `pause for half a second before retrying`

  e.g. `render %template%, error=%error%, write to %text%`
  e.g. `render 'layout.html'`

  e.g. `set %timeout% = "PT30S"`

  e.g. `set %version% = "2.0"`
  e.g. `set %iso%(duration) = "PT5M"`
  e.g. `set %doc% = "2026-01-01" as text`
  e.g. `set %img% = "real.gif" as image/gif strict`
  e.g. `set %n% = "42" as int`
  e.g. `get 'https://example.com/rates.json', write to %rates%`
  e.g. `hash %password%, write to %passwordHash%`
  e.g. `call GetUser id=%userId%, write to %user%`
  e.g. `sort %names%, write to %sortedNames%`
- goal.call: Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
  e.g. `call Finalize`
  e.g. `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
  e.g. `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
- loop.foreach: Iterate over Collection, binding each element to Item (and its key or index to Key) and executing the remaining step actions
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call ProcessItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `foreach %rows%, write out %row%`
  e.g. `foreach %products% as %product%, call Handle`
  e.g. `foreach %prices% as %price% with key %sku%, write out "%sku%: %price%"`
- goal.return: Return early from the current goal, propagating Data as the goal result
  e.g. `return %result%`
  e.g. `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
  e.g. `if %items% is empty, return`
- output.write: Write Data to a named channel — defaults to the actor's output channel.
  e.g. `write out "Welcome back, %user.name%"`
  e.g. `show %message% to the user`
  e.g. `print %result%`
  e.g. `write %error.Message% to "errors" channel`
- on.error: Answer when the action before it fails; optionally retry it, run a recovery, or carry on past the error
  e.g. `read file.txt, on error call HandleMissing`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `save %doc%, on error key Conflict, write out "already exists"`
  e.g. `read %path%, on error 404, write out "missing"`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times`
  e.g. `http get %url%, on error retry 3 times over 30 seconds`
  e.g. `write out "hi", on error ignore`
  e.g. `call Save, on error retry 2 times, then call Rollback`
  e.g. `call Save, on error call Rollback first, then retry 2 times`
  e.g. `render %template%, on error 404 call Fallback then retry, write to %text%`
- on.cache: Cache the result of the action before it for a duration; a cached result answers in its place and the work is skipped
  e.g. `get https://example.com/rates, cache for 5 minutes, write to %rates%`
  e.g. `read %path%, cache 1 hour sliding`
  e.g. `call LoadUser id=%id%, cache 10 minutes by "user-%id%"`
- on.timeout: Give the action before it a deadline; past it the action is cancelled and fails with a Timeout (408) error
  e.g. `get %url%, timeout after 10 seconds`
  e.g. `call Import, timeout 2 minutes, on error call Alert`
- condition.if: Evaluate a condition and execute the then-branch actions; pair with elseif/else for full branching
  e.g. `if %count% > 0, call ProcessItems`
  e.g. `if %content% is not empty`
  e.g. `if %flag% is true, call Go`
  e.g. `if %done%, return %result%`
- file.read: Read a file's content; optionally resolve %var% patterns in the text before returning
  e.g. `read file.txt, write to %content%`
  e.g. `read 'config/settings.json'`

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Start. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="goalHeader", goal=%goal%
step 1: set %buildStart% = %Now.Ticks%
step 2: set %trace% = {"id": "%!trace.id%", "timestamp": "%Now%", "goal": %goal%, "menu": null, "subGoals": [], "durationMs": 0}
step 3: call Compile, on error call HandleBuildFailure
step 4: set %trace.menu% = %menu%

Types
- text — Textual content. Kind is set from the file extension (md, txt, csv, html, ...). Kind is a hint by default; strict is a no-op for text (plain vs markdown is not detectable from content). (e.g. Hello, world)
- number — A number, whole or decimal, of any size. Its kind is the precision it is held in (int, long, decimal, double, …). (e.g. 42)
- bool — True or false. (e.g. true)
- list — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- dict — Named values: each key holds a value of any type. (e.g. {"name":"Ada","age":36})
- variable — A variable, named between % signs, that holds a value. (e.g. %user%)
- item
- choice<actor> — one of: system, user

## variable.set(Name: variable, Value: item, Type?: item, AsDefault?: bool = false)
Assign a value to a named variable, optionally coercing to a type or setting only when unset
Name — the variable to set, with its % signs. A `(<kind>)` written after it is not part of the name: it is the Type.
Value — the value as the step writes it, typed as what it is (a quoted date is a date, "42" a number, a label stays text). After another action in the same step it is %!data%.
Type — only when the step forces a type: `as <type>` or `(<kind>)`.
AsDefault — true when the step says "set default", "default to" or "only if unset"; the variable keeps a value it already has.

- `set %x% = …` is one variable.set.
- `<action>, write to %x%` is that action followed by variable.set(Name=%x%, Value=%!data%) — its own action, never a modifier, and without a Type.

## loop.foreach(Collection: item, Item?: variable = item, Key?: variable)
Iterate over Collection, binding each element to Item (and its key or index to Key) and executing the remaining step actions
Collection — the list or dict to walk.
Item — the variable each element is bound to; %item% unless the step names another (`as %product%`).
Key — the variable the key or index is bound to, only when the step names one (`with key %sku%`).

- The work done per element is its own action after loop.foreach in the step's list (usually goal.call), never inside it.
- `name=%item%` after the called goal is an argument of that goal.call, not a foreach property.

## goal.call(Name: text, Parameter?: list, Actor?: choice<actor>, Parallel?: bool = false)
Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
Name — the goal to call, copied exactly as the step writes it: `Goal`, `Folder/Goal`, `/system/builder/Goal`. Never an action name like `goal.call`.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the goal name is one argument, its value as written. Left out when the step passes none.
Actor — the actor the goal runs on, only when the step names one (`on actor "system"`, `as user`). Not because the goal is a system goal, a sub-goal or a recovery.
Parallel — true only when the step says the call may run beside others.

- The arguments belong to the called goal; they are never properties of goal.call.
- `foreach %list%, call X item=%y%` is loop.foreach, then goal.call with `item` as its argument.

## ui.render(Template: text, Parameter?: list, IsFile?: bool)
Render a Liquid template (file or inline) with the current variables and optional explicit parameters
Template — the template as the step names it: a file path or the template text itself.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the template is one argument, the same as goal.call's (`render x.html, name=%name%, n=5` → name and n). Left out when the step passes none.
IsFile — only when the step says so: `inline` / `as text` → false, `from file` → true. Otherwise left out; the render finds out itself.

## llm.decider(State: text, Question: dict, Model?: text = jev-latest)
Ask a decision service a set of typed questions about one shared state and get an answer for each — a yes/no probability, or a pick from a closed set of options
State — the shared context every question is asked against.
Question — the questions to answer.
Model — the decision model, only when the step names one.

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

How plang is structured:
- A goal is a list of steps. Each step is a sentence saying what to do, written in any human language. There is no syntax and no reserved words; only the intent matters.
- A step is carried out by one or more actions. Every action belongs to exactly one module.
- Within a step the actions form a chain: the result of one action can feed the next one.
- A step may keep its result for later use by naming a variable (a name between % signs). That is the variable module's job, in addition to whatever module did the work.
- A step may guard part of its work behind a condition (condition module), repeat part of it for each item of a collection (loop module), or attach error handling to it (error module). Each of those is an action of its own, and whatever runs INSIDE the guard, the loop or the error handler is also an action of its own — so calling a goal inside an if, a loop or an error handler uses the goal module as well.
- So one step often uses several modules: the one doing the main work; condition/loop/error for a surrounding clause; goal when a goal is called anywhere in it; variable when the result is kept.
- A module counts as used by a step whenever the step's sentence names work that module does, EVEN IF that work only runs in some cases — the body of a condition, of a loop, or of an error handler is named by the step and counts, regardless of whether it happens to run.
- A step that REGISTERS something to happen later — an event handler, a callback, a scheduled goal — does not do that work now. Naming a goal to be run later is not calling it; the step uses the module that does the registering.
- Steps are listed in order and may be indented. An indented step is the body of the step above it, and belongs to that step; each step is still asked about on its own, for what its own sentence does.

This is a plang goal called Decide. Its steps are numbered from 0.

step 0: set %threshold% = 0.5
step 1: set %modules% = %!app.module.list%
step 2: set %state.goal% = %goal.Name%
step 3: foreach %goal.Step%, call AddStepToState step=%item%
step 4: foreach %modules%, call AddModuleToState module=%item%
step 5: render template "/system/builder/llm/templates/deciderModuleQuestions.template", write to %moduleQuestions%
step 6: llm.decider State=%state%, Question=%moduleQuestions%, write to %moduleAnswer%
step 7: render template "/system/builder/llm/templates/deciderActionQuestions.template", write to %actionQuestions%
step 8: llm.decider State=%state%, Question=%actionQuestions%, write to %actionAnswer%
step 9: call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="goal-decided", goal=%goal%

These are the plang modules you may choose from:
- build: Builder internals: load, merge, validate, and save goal and step data during the build pipeline
  action build.appSave: Persist the built app artifact to disk after a successful build run
  action build.fold: Place the steps indented under a condition into that condition's child, in the goal and its sub-goals
  action build.goals: Load all goal files from a directory for processing by the builder
  action build.goalsSave: Save a built goal's .pr file to disk, completing the build for that goal
  action build.load: Load the app-level build context from a directory path
  action build.match: Check the LLM's answer against the goal's steps, one entry per step, before the steps take their actions from it
  action build.pick: Hand a decider answer to each step of a goal, which works out the actions the decider picked for it
- goal: Goals: call another goal (`call X`, on its own or as the body of an if/foreach/on-error clause) and return from the current goal
  e.g. `call Finalize`
  e.g. `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
  e.g. `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
  e.g. `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
  e.g. `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
  e.g. `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
  e.g. `return %result%`
  e.g. `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
  e.g. `if %items% is empty, return`
  action goal.call: Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
    examples: `goal.call` runs another goal. It is the action behind `call X` wherever that clause appears — on its own, as the body of a condition, as the body of a loop, or inside an error handler. `Name` is the goal; each named argument after it is one row in `Parameter`.

Step text: `call Finalize`
Properties: `{"Name": "Finalize"}`

Step text: `call ProcessOrder id=%orderId%, retries=3`
Properties: `{"Name": "ProcessOrder", "Parameter": [{"name": "id", "value": "%orderId%"}, {"name": "retries", "value": 3}]}`

Step text: `call /system/builder/EmitBuildEvent kind="done"`
Properties: `{"Name": "/system/builder/EmitBuildEvent", "Parameter": [{"name": "kind", "value": "done"}]}` — a path-qualified name is still just the name.

Step text: `if %total% > 5, call MarkBig`
Properties: `{"Name": "MarkBig"}` — the condition is its own action; this one is only the call.

Step text: `foreach %items%, call HandleItem item=%item%`
Properties: `{"Name": "HandleItem", "Parameter": [{"name": "item", "value": "%item%"}]}` — the loop is its own action.

Step text: `verify %data% with contracts ['C1'], on error call HandleContractError`
Properties: `{"Name": "HandleContractError"}` — a goal called inside an error handler is an ordinary call.
  action goal.return: Return early from the current goal, propagating Data as the goal result
    examples: Step text: `return %result%`
Properties: `{"Data": "%result%"}`

Step text: `if %goal.IsCached%, return %goal.Cache%`
Properties: `{"Data": "%goal.Cache%"}` — the return is the if's body: it goes inside the if's `{ }`, `condition.if(Left=%goal.IsCached%) { goal.return(Data=%goal.Cache%) }`, never beside the if.

Step text: `if %items% is empty, return`
Properties: `{}` — a return that names no value; the body of the if: `condition.if(Left=%items%, Operator="isempty") { goal.return() }`.
- llm: Send prompts to an LLM and receive structured or streamed responses, with optional tool use; or ask a decision service typed yes/no and pick-one questions about a shared state
  e.g. `system: analyze sentiment, user: %comment%, schema: {sentiment: string}, write to %result%`
  e.g. `ask the llm "summarise %text%", write to %summary%`
  action llm.decider: Ask a decision service a set of typed questions about one shared state and get an answer for each — a yes/no probability, or a pick from a closed set of options
  action llm.query: Send a conversation (system + user messages) to an LLM and return the response, with optional schema or tool use
    examples: Step text: `system: analyze sentiment, user: %comment%, schema: {sentiment: string}, write to %result%`
Properties: `{"Message": [{"Role": "system", "Content": "analyze sentiment"}, {"Role": "user", "Content": "%comment%"}], "Schema": {"sentiment": "string"}}`

Step text: `ask the llm "summarise %text%", write to %summary%`
Properties: `{"Message": [{"Role": "user", "Content": "summarise %text%"}]}` — a step with no system part is one user message.
- ui: Render Liquid templates from inline content or files with PLang variable injection
  e.g. `render 'page.html' with title=%pageTitle%, write to %html%`
  e.g. `render %template%, error=%error%, write to %text%`
  e.g. `render 'layout.html'`
  action ui.render: Render a Liquid template (file or inline) with the current variables and optional explicit parameters
    examples: Step text: `render 'page.html' with title=%pageTitle%, write to %html%`
Properties: `{"Template": "page.html", "Parameter": {title: %pageTitle%}}`

Step text: `render %template%, error=%error%, write to %text%`
Properties: `{"Template": "%template%", "Parameter": {error: %error%}}` — every `name=value` after the template is an argument, even when the value is a variable of the same name: `ui.render(Template=%template%, Parameter={error: %error%})`.

Step text: `render 'layout.html'`
Properties: `{"Template": "layout.html"}`

Types
- text — Textual content. Kind is set from the file extension (md, txt, csv, html, ...). Kind is a hint by default; strict is a no-op for text (plain vs markdown is not detectable from content). (e.g. Hello, world)
- number — A number, whole or decimal, of any size. Its kind is the precision it is held in (int, long, decimal, double, …). (e.g. 42)
- bool — True or false. (e.g. true)
- list — An ordered list of values, each of any type. (e.g. [1, 2, 3])
- dict — Named values: each key holds a value of any type. (e.g. {"name":"Ada","age":36})
- variable — A variable, named between % signs, that holds a value. (e.g. %user%)
- item
- choice<operator> — one of: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, contains, notcontains, startswith, notstartswith, endswith, notendswith, in, notin, isempty, isnotempty, is, isnot, and, or
- choice<actor> — one of: system, user
- choice<overflow> — one of: Promote, Throw
- choice<precision> — one of: Error, Double, Decimal

## list.count(ListName: variable)
Return the number of items in the list
ListName — the list to count, with its % signs.

## variable.set(Name: variable, Value: item, Type?: item, AsDefault?: bool = false)
Assign a value to a named variable, optionally coercing to a type or setting only when unset
Name — the variable to set, with its % signs. A `(<kind>)` written after it is not part of the name: it is the Type.
Value — the value as the step writes it, typed as what it is (a quoted date is a date, "42" a number, a label stays text). After another action in the same step it is %!data%.
Type — only when the step forces a type: `as <type>` or `(<kind>)`.
AsDefault — true when the step says "set default", "default to" or "only if unset"; the variable keeps a value it already has.

- `set %x% = …` is one variable.set.
- `<action>, write to %x%` is that action followed by variable.set(Name=%x%, Value=%!data%) — its own action, never a modifier, and without a Type.

## output.write(Data: item, channel?: text)
Write Data to a named channel — defaults to the actor's output channel.
Data — what to write, as the step writes it: a quoted text (with or without %variables% in it) is text, a bare %variable% is item.
channel — the name of a registered channel to write to, only when the step names one (`to "log" channel`, `on X channel`, `via X`). Left out otherwise: the actor's output.

- Naming a channel routes the output; it never registers one (that is channel.set).

## condition.if(Left: item, Operator?: choice<operator>, Right?: item)
Evaluate a condition and execute the then-branch actions; pair with elseif/else for full branching
Left — the value tested, as the step writes it.
Operator — the comparison, one of choice<operator>. A negation is its own operator, never written anywhere else. Left out when the step names only Left: then the condition is Left's own truth.
Right — what Left is compared to. Left out for isempty / isnotempty, and when Operator is.

| the step says | Operator | Right |
|---|---|---|
| `if %x%` alone (is it true, does it exist, is it set) | left out | left out |
| `is 5`, `equals %b%`, `is "x"`, `is true`, `is null` | == | the value |
| `is not 5`, `does not equal %b%`, `is not null` | != | the value |
| `is less than`, `is more than`, `is at least`, `is at most` | <, >, >=, <= | the value |
| `contains` / `does not contain` | contains / notcontains | the value |
| `starts with` / `does not start with` | startswith / notstartswith | the value |
| `ends with` / `does not end with` | endswith / notendswith | the value |
| `is in [..]` / `is not in [..]` | in / notin | the list |
| `is empty` / `is not empty` | isempty / isnotempty | left out |
| `is a number` / `is not a list` | is / isnot | the type name: number, list |

- `is` and `isnot` take only a type name; a value after "is" is `==`.
- There is no istrue, isfalse, isnull or isnotnull.
- `if A and B`: one condition.if cannot hold both. Compare each side with condition.compare, keep each result with variable.set, then one condition.if over the two with Operator `and` (or `or`).

## condition.elseif(Left: item, Operator?: choice<operator>, Right?: item)
Additional condition branch evaluated when the preceding if condition is false
Left, Operator, Right — the same as condition.if's.

- Right after the if (or another elseif) of the same step: `…, else if %x% is 1, …`.

## condition.else()
Fallback branch that executes when all preceding if/elseif conditions are false
No properties: it runs its child when no branch before it held.

- Right after the if or elseif of the same step.

## error.throw(Message?: text, Data?: item, StatusCode?: number = 400, Key?: text = error, FixSuggestion?: text)
Immediately fail the step with a structured error message, status code, and optional key
Message — the error's message: the quoted text after `throw`.
Data — the values the error carries: the %variables% after `throw` (`throw %!error%` re-raises that error).
StatusCode — the status code, only when the step gives one.
Key — the error's key, only when the step names one.
FixSuggestion — how the programmer fixes it: the text after `fix suggestion`.

## goal.call(Name: text, Parameter?: list, Actor?: choice<actor>, Parallel?: bool = false)
Call a named goal, injecting parameters into its context, optionally on a different actor
Name — the goal to call, copied exactly as the step writes it: `Goal`, `Folder/Goal`, `/system/builder/Goal`. Never an action name like `goal.call`.
Parameter — the arguments: every `name=value` after the goal name is one argument, its value as written. Left out when the step passes none.
Actor — the actor the goal runs on, only when the step names one (`on actor "system"`, `as user`). Not because the goal is a system goal, a sub-goal or a recovery.
Parallel — true only when the step says the call may run beside others.

- The arguments belong to the called goal; they are never properties of goal.call.
- `foreach %list%, call X item=%y%` is loop.foreach, then goal.call with `item` as its argument.

## math.multiply(A: item, B: item, Overflow?: choice<overflow> = Promote, Precision?: choice<precision> = Error)
Multiply A by B and return the numeric result
A, B — the two numbers: the result is A × B.
Overflow — only when the step says what to do when an integer overflows: Promote widens it, Throw fails.
Precision — only when the step says how to mix a decimal and a floating-point number.

## list.add(ListName: variable, Value: item, AtIndex?: number = -1)
Append or insert a value into a list variable at an optional index
ListName — the list variable to add to, with its % signs: in `add X to %list%` it is %list%.
Value — what to add, as the step writes it; a `{…}` or `[…]` literal is one value, typed dict or list.
AtIndex — the position to insert at, only when the step names one ("at position 2"); otherwise it appends.

- `add X to %list%` has no variable.set: %list% is the target, not a result to keep.
